Subject: PioneerWell SLA measurement & credit calculation — initial proposal

Hi Sophia / PioneerWell procurement team,

Thanks again for the RFP. Attached is a concise SLA proposal that covers availability, latency SLOs, measurement methodology, and the proposed service credit calculation. Highlights: 
- Availability: 99.95% monthly availability (region-weighted).
- Latency: p95 < 250ms, p99 < 700ms for standard generation routes (exclusions detailed).
- Measurement: combination of production telemetry (server-side sampling) + synthetic probe coverage; probe weighting and burst-window handling described in Appendix A.
- Credits: tiered credits with a capped monthly maximum; example calculations included.

Next steps: please review the attached PDF and Appendix CSV and flag any items you want to discuss. If helpful, we can run a short workshop to walk the measurement examples.

Attachments: 20281116-pioneerwell-sla-proposal.pdf (PDF, 6 pages); pw-sla-measurement-appendix.csv (measurement examples)

Marcus — thanks for sending. A few clarifying questions before we circle back to procurement: 
1) Burst windows: your Appendix references a 5-minute burst window for transient spikes. Can you confirm how that interacts with sustained degradation (e.g., repeated 30-second spikes every 6 minutes)? How are those aggregated into the monthly availability calculation?
2) Synthetic probes vs production telemetry: what weight do you apply to each source when they conflict? Is there an adjudication process?
3) Evidence: procurement will require a sample evidence pack showing the telemetry used to compute one month of availability (redacted). Can you provide that?

We'd also like a DocuSign-ready SLA once we settle language.

Thanks,
Sophia Thompson
Head of Platform Operations, PioneerWell
sophia.thompson@pioneerwell.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com
Date: 2028-11-16T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: PioneerWell SLA measurement & credit calculation — initial proposal

Forwarding Sophia's questions — procurement wants clarity on burst-window aggregation, probe weighting, and an evidence pack. Draft response below (will send to PioneerWell once you OK):

--- Draft reply ---
We treat burst windows as short-duration tolerances: isolated and narrowly-scoped deviations shorter than 5 minutes are classified as transient and only count toward availability when their frequency exceeds the sustained threshold (defined as >3 occurrences within a 1-hour rolling window). For repeated short spikes (your example), if occurrences cause >0.5% of requests to exceed the SLO across the month, they escalate into sustained degradation and are included in the monthly availability calculation.

Synthetic probes are used to detect customer-visible surface-level failures and ensure region coverage; production telemetry is the primary measurement for per-customer request-level SLOs. When measurements disagree, we use a simple adjudication: if production telemetry indicates a degradation that is not reflected in probes, we prioritize production telemetry and include the incident; if probes detect a cross-region connectivity issue not seen in production sampling, we open an investigation and may include probe-derived evidence only after correlation. We propose a 70/30 production-to-probe weighting by default, with adjustments contractually agreed for highly synthetic-dependent deployments.

We can provide a redacted evidence pack (sample month) showing raw telemetry, probe traces, and the calculation workbook.

--- End draft ---

Lauren — can you confirm legal is comfortable with the >3 occurrences / 1-hour rolling window language and the 70/30 weighting? Karthik — can you add a short note on how our telemetry sampling bias is corrected and how we normalize for traffic volume (we referenced this in Appendix A but the customer will likely ask more).

Thanks,
Marcus

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com
Date: 2028-11-16T12:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: PioneerWell SLA measurement & credit calculation — initial proposal

Thanks for the draft — a few quick edits from procurement/legal perspective: 
- Service credit matrix: make the tiers explicit with concrete dollar-credit calculations tied to monthly invoice; include a hard cap equal to 50% of monthly hosting fees.
- Latency SLOs: call out p95 for interactive paths and p99 only for bulk/generative jobs; customers often try to push p99 on every route which is operationally different.
- Adjudication: add an appeal path — customer can request a 14-day audit where we share the redacted telemetry, and an independent third-party (mutually agreed) can be engaged if disputes persist.

Karthik — re: sampling normalization, please add a paragraph we can include in Appendix A explaining our inverse-probability sampling correction and how we collapse short-lived connection errors to avoid double-counting. If you can drop that text into the Appendix CSV and mark examples, I'll incorporate and send the updated packet.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Procurement Programs, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.inference.com

Sophia — thanks for the quick review and great questions. Attached are the updated proposal PDF and Appendix CSV which incorporate: 
- Explicit service credit tiers + capped-credit language (cap = 50% of monthly hosting fees).
- Burst-window clarification: 5-minute transient window, escalation threshold >3 occurrences in 1 hour as described.
- Measurement weighting: default 70% production telemetry / 30% synthetic probe; adjudication process and 14-day audit/third-party appeal path included.
- Sampling normalization paragraph added to Appendix A with an example row.

Links: Confluence walkthrough: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/PW-SLA-2028; DocuSign (placeholder) https://www.docusign.com/en/contract/abcdef1234567890
